title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 91 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 494–496 (Night 91, continuing directly from nights-90), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 91 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Sharrukān and Ḍawʾ al-Makān take counsel after the first day’s fighting; Sharrukān sends the chamberlain and the vizier Dandān with twenty thousand horsemen to hide near the shore and take the Christians in the rear, and the Muslim army feigns flight to draw the enemy on. King Afrīdūn, thinking the day won, sends a boastful message to the king of the Rūm, and Shahrazād is cut off by dawn as the Christians cry out for vengeance. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْحَادِيَةُ وَالتِّسْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-ḥādiyatu wa-al-tisʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the one-and-ninetieth,
sentences.i: And when it was the ninety-first night,
sentences.n: The night is numbered “the one-and-ninetieth”: the ordinal for one-and-ninety is formed with the ‘first’ (ḥādī) ordinal and wa-, ‘and’.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْكُفَّارَ لَمَّا رَأَوْا لُوقَا بْنَ شَمْلُوطَ وَقَعَ مَقْتُولًا لَطَمُوا عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ وَنَادَوْا بِالْوَيْلِ وَالثُّبُورِ وَاسْتَغَاثُوا بِبَطَارِقَةِ الدُّيُورِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-kuffāra lammā raʾaw lūqā ibna shamlūṭa waqaʿa maqtūlan laṭamū ʿalā wujūhihim wa-nādaw bi-al-waylī wa-al-thubūri wa-istaghāthū bi-baṭāriqati al-duyūri
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the unbelievers, when they saw Lūqā son of Shamlūṭ fallen slain, struck upon their faces, and cried out with woe and with perdition, and called for help on the patriarchs of the monasteries,
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the unbelievers saw Lūqā son of Shamlūṭ fallen dead, they beat their faces, cried out “Woe and ruin!” and called on the patriarchs of the monasteries for help,
sentences.n: The print runs السعيد and أن together (السعيدان); they are read as two words, and the join is kept. The name is printed شملوط here and شلموط in the night before; the print varies, and both are kept as printed. The night opens by repeating the last sentence of the one before.

sentences.t: وَقَالُوا أَيْنَ الصُّلْبَانُ وَتَزَهُّدُ الرُّهْبَانِ ثُمَّ اجْتَمَعُوا جَمِيعًا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālū ayna al-ṣulbānu wa-tazahhudu al-ruhbāni thumma ijtamaʿū jamīʿan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: and said: Where are the crosses, and the ascetic-practice of the monks? Then they gathered, all together, upon him,
sentences.i: and said, “Where are the crosses now, and the self-denial of the monks?” Then they all massed against him,
sentences.n: وتزهد الرهبان is obscure as printed; it is read as ‘and the monks’ self-denial’, a taunt at gods and holy men who have failed them. The ‘him’ is Sharrukān.

sentences.t: وَأَعْمَلُوا الصَّوَارِمَ وَالرِّمَاحَ وَهَجَمُوا لِلْحَرْبِ وَالْكِفَاحِ وَالْتَقَتِ الْعَسَاكِرُ بِالْعَسَاكِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿmalū al-ṣawārima wa-al-rimāḥa wa-hajamū li-al-ḥarbi wa-al-kifāḥi wa-iltaqati al-ʿasākiru bi-al-ʿasākiri
sentences.l: and put-to-work the swords and the lances, and rushed to the war and the combat, and the armies met with the armies,
sentences.i: They plied sword and lance, rushed into the fight and the combat, and army met army,
sentences.n: The print has واعلموا, a misprint for واعملوا, corrected here (the printed word would mean ‘and they informed’).

sentences.t: وَصَارَتِ الصُّدُورُ تَحْتَ وَقْعِ الْحَوَافِرِ وَتَحَكَّمَتِ الرِّمَاحُ وَالصَّوَارِمُ وَضَعُفَتِ السَّوَاعِدُ وَالْمَعَاصِمُ وَكَأَنَّ الْخَيْلَ قَدْ خُلِقَتْ بِلَا قَوَائِمَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārati al-ṣudūru taḥta waqʿi al-ḥawāfiri wa-taḥakkamati al-rimāḥu wa-al-ṣawārimu wa-ḍaʿufati al-sawāʿidu wa-al-maʿāṣimu wa-ka-anna al-khayla qad khuliqat bi-lā qawāʾima
sentences.l: and the breasts became beneath the striking of the hooves, and the lances and the swords held sway, and the forearms and the wrists grew weak, and as if the horses had been created without legs,
sentences.i: Chests lay under the pounding of hooves, lances and swords held sway, forearms and wrists grew weak, and it was as though the horses had been made without legs,
sentences.n: The print has وكان, which is read as وكأنّ ‘and as if’ (the same consonants as ‘and it was’); the sense — horses that cannot move out of the press — wants ‘as if’.

sentences.t: وَلَازَالَ مُنَادِي الْحَرْبِ يُنَادِي إِلَى أَنْ كَلَّتِ الْأَيَادِي وَذَهَبَ النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالِاعْتِكَارِ وَافْتَرَقَ الْجَيْشَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-lāzāla munādī al-ḥarbi yunādī ilā an kallati al-ayādī wa-dhahaba al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri wa-iftaraqa al-jayshāni
sentences.l: and the crier of the war did not cease calling until the hands grew weary, and the day went, and the night came on with the thick-darkness, and the two armies parted,
sentences.i: The herald of war kept calling until hands grew weary, the day was gone, night came on in thickening darkness, and the two armies drew apart,
sentences.n: The print joins ولا and زال (ولازال, ‘and he did not cease’); the join is kept. بالاعتكار: iʿtikār is dense, gathering darkness.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ كُلُّ شُجَاعٍ كَالسَّكْرَانِ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الضَّرْبِ وَالطِّعَانِ وَقَدِ امْتَلَأَتِ الْأَرْضُ بِالْقَتْلَى وَعَظُمَتِ الْجِرَاحَاتُ وَلَايَعْرِفُ الْجَرِيحُ مِمَّنْ مَاتَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra kullu shujāʿin ka-al-sakrāni min shiddati al-ḍarbi wa-al-ṭiʿāni wa-qadi imtalaʾati al-arḍu bi-al-qatlā wa-ʿaẓamati al-jirāḥātu wa-lāyaʿrifu al-jarīḥu mimman māta
sentences.l: and every brave-man became like the drunk from the severity of the striking and the thrusting, and the earth had been filled with the slain, and the wounds grew great, and the wounded-one did not know [himself] from those-who died.
sentences.i: Every brave man reeled like a drunkard from the force of the blows and thrusts. The earth was filled with the slain, the wounds were grievous, and the wounded could not be told from the dead.
sentences.n: The print joins لا and يعرف (ولايعرف); the join is kept. The last clause is elliptic: the wounded man cannot tell himself from those who have died, or cannot be told from them.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ شَرْكَانَ اجْتَمَعَ بِأَخِيهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَالْحَاجِبِ وَالْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ لِأَخِيهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَالْحَاجِبِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ فَتَحَ بَابًا لِهَلَاكِ الْكَافِرِينَ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna sharrukāna ijtamaʿa bi-akhīhi ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-al-ḥājibi wa-al-wazīri dandāna fa-qāla sharrukānu li-akhīhi ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-al-ḥājibi inna allāha qad fataḥa bāban li-halāki al-kāfirīna wa-al-ḥamdu li-allāhi rabbi al-ʿālamīna
sentences.l: Then Sharrukān met with his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the chamberlain and the vizier Dandān, and Sharrukān said to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and to the chamberlain: Truly God has opened a door to the destruction of the unbelievers, and praise be to God, lord of the worlds.
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān met with his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, the chamberlain and the vizier Dandān, and said to his brother and the chamberlain: God has opened a door to the destruction of the unbelievers, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.
sentences.n: The print has والحمد الله, a misprint for والحمد لله, corrected here (the lām of ‘to God’ was dropped). الحمد لله رب العالمين is the opening of the Qurʾān, the standard formula of thanks.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ لِأَخِيهِ لَمْ نَزَلْ نَحْمَدُ اللَّهَ لِكَشْفِ الْكَرْبِ عَنِ الْعَرَبِ وَالْعَجَمِ وَسَوْفَ تَتَحَدَّثُ النَّاسُ جِيلًا بَعْدَ جِيلٍ بِمَا صَنَعْتَ بِاللَّعِينِ لُوقَا مُحَرِّفِ الْإِنْجِيلِ وَأَخْذِكَ الْحَرْبَةَ مِنَ الْهَوَى وَضَرْبِكَ لِعَدُوِّاللَّهِ بَيْنَ الْوَرَى وَيَبْقَى حَدِيثُكَ إِلَى آخِرِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni li-akhīhi lam nazal naḥmadu allāha li-kashfi al-karbi ʿani al-ʿarabi wa-al-ʿajami wa-sawfa tataḥaddathu al-nāsu jīlan baʿda jīlin bi-mā ṣanaʿta bi-al-laʿīni lūqā muḥarrifi al-injīli wa-akhdhika al-ḥarbata mina al-hawā wa-ḍarbika li-ʿaduwwi-allāhi bayna al-warā wa-yabqā ḥadīthuka ilā ākhiri al-zamāni
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to his brother: We have not ceased praising God for the uncovering of the distress from the Arabs and the non-Arabs; and the people will talk, generation after generation, of what you did to the accursed Lūqā, the falsifier of the Gospel, and your taking the spear from the air, and your striking the enemy-of-God before the creatures; and your story will remain until the last of time.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to his brother: We have never stopped thanking God for lifting this distress from Arab and non-Arab alike. People will talk, generation after generation, of what you did to the accursed Lūqā, the corrupter of the Gospel — how you took the spear from the air and struck down God’s enemy before the eyes of the world — and your story will last until the end of time.
sentences.n: The print joins لعدو and الله (لعدوالله); the join is kept. محرّف الإنجيل: Muslim polemic holds that Christians altered the Gospel text.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ شَرْكَانُ أَيُّهَا الْحَاجِبُ الْكَبِيرُ وَالْمِقْدَامُ الْخَطِيرُ فَأَجَابَهُ بِالتَّلْبِيَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ خُذْ مَعَكَ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ وَعِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ وَسَرِّبْهُمْ إِلَى نَاحِيَةِ الْبَحْرِ مِقْدَارَ سَبْعَةِ فَرَاسِخَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla sharrukānu ayyuhā al-ḥājibu al-kabīru wa-al-miqdāmu al-khaṭīru fa-ajābahu bi-al-talbiyati fa-qāla lahu khudh maʿaka al-wazīra dandāna wa-ʿishrīna alfa fārisin wa-sarribhum ilā nāḥiyati al-baḥri miqdāra sabʿati farāsikha
sentences.l: Then Sharrukān said: O chamberlain the great, and the dauntless-one the weighty — and he answered him with the response — and he said to him: Take with you the vizier Dandān and twenty thousand horsemen, and send them in-companies to the side of the sea, the measure of seven leagues,
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān said, “O great chamberlain, O dauntless and mighty one,” and the chamberlain answered, “At your service.” He said to him: Take with you the vizier Dandān and twenty thousand horsemen, and lead them in small bands toward the sea, some seven leagues,
sentences.n: التلبية is the answering cry لبيك, ‘at your service’. سرّبهم: to send men off in files or companies; the print leaves the shadda unmarked, so the form is read by sense. A farsakh (league) is about three miles.

sentences.t: وَأَسْرِعُوا فِى السَّيْرِ حَتَّى تَكُونُوا قَرِيبًا مِنَ السَّاحِلِ بِحَيْثُ يَبْقَى بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ قَدْرُ فَرْسَخَيْنِ وَاخْتَفُوا فِي وَهَدَاتِ الْأَرْضِ حَتَّى تَسْمَعُوا ضَجَّةَ الْكُفَّارِ إِذَا طَلَعُوا مِنَ الْمَرَاكِبِ وَتَسْمَعُوا الصِّيَاحَ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ وَقَدْ عَمِلَتْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمُ الْقَوَاضِبُ
sentences.tr: wa-asriʿū fī al-sayri ḥattā takūnū qarīban mina al-sāḥili bi-ḥaythu yabqā baynakum wa-bayna al-qawmi qadru farsakhayni wa-ikhtafū fī wahadāti al-arḍi ḥattā tasmaʿū ḍajjata al-kuffāri idhā ṭalaʿū mina al-marākibi wa-tasmaʿū al-ṣiyāḥa min kulli jānibin wa-qad ʿamilat baynanā wa-baynahumu al-qawāḍibu
sentences.l: and hasten in the going until you are near to the shore, in such-a-way that there remains between you and the people the measure of two leagues, and hide in the hollows of the earth until you hear the clamour of the unbelievers when they come up out of the ships, and hear the shouting from every side, and the cutting-swords have worked between us and them.
sentences.i: Make haste on the way until you are close to the shore, leaving about two leagues between you and the enemy. Hide in the folds of the ground until you hear the din of the unbelievers coming up from the ships and the shouting on every side, with the swords already at work between us and them.
sentences.n: The print spells فى (with ى) here and في (with ي) a few words on; both are kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا رَأَيْتُمْ عَسْكَرَنَا تَقَهْقَرُوا إِلَى وَرَاءٍ كَأَنَّهُمْ مُنْهَزِمُونَ وَجَاءَتِ الْكُفَّارُ زَاحِفَةً خَلْفَهُمْ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْجِهَاتِ حَتَّى مِنْ جَانِبِ السَّاحِلِ وَالْخِيَامِ فَكُونُوا لَهُمْ بِالْمِرْصَادِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhā raʾaytum ʿaskaranā taqahqarū ilā warāʾin ka-annahum munhazimūna wa-jāʾati al-kuffāru zāḥifatan khalfahum min jamīʿi al-jihāti ḥattā min jānibi al-sāḥili wa-al-khiyāmi fa-kūnū lahum bi-al-mirṣādi
sentences.l: So when you see our army fallen-back to the rear, as if they were routed, and the unbelievers have come creeping behind them from all sides, even from the side of the shore and of the tents, then be for them in the ambush.
sentences.i: When you see our army fall back as though routed, and the unbelievers come creeping after them from every side, even from the shore and the tents, lie in wait for them.
sentences.n: تقهقروا is printed as a perfect (‘they have fallen back’) after ‘when you see’, which strictly wants the imperfect; it is read by sense. بالمرصاد: ‘in ambush’.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ أَنْتَ عَلَمًا عَلَيْهِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَارْفَعِ الْعَلَمَ الْأَخْضَرَ وَصِحْ قَائِلًا اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَاحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ وَرَائِهِمْ وَاجْتَهِدْ فِي أَنْ لَا يَحُولَ الْكُفَّارُ بَيْنَ الْمُنْهَزِمِينَ وَبَيْنَ الْبَحْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā raʾayta anta ʿalaman ʿalayhi lā ilāha illā allāhu muḥammadun rasūlu allāhi ṣallā allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama fa-irfaʿi al-ʿalama al-akhḍara wa-ṣiḥ qāʾilan allāhu akbaru wa-iḥmil ʿalayhim min warāʾihim wa-ijtahid fī an lā yaḥūla al-kuffāru bayna al-munhazimīna wa-bayna al-baḥri
sentences.l: And when you yourself see a banner with on it There is no god but God, Muḥammad is the messenger of God, God bless him and give him peace, raise the green banner and cry out saying God is greatest, and charge upon them from behind them, and strive that the unbelievers not come between the routed and the sea.
sentences.i: And when you see a banner bearing There is no god but God, Muḥammad is the messenger of God, God bless him and give him peace, raise the green banner and cry out God is greatest! Charge them from behind, and take care that the unbelievers do not cut the fleeing men off from the sea.
sentences.n: The print marks the vowels on عَلَما (the banner) itself. In the second clause the ‘routed’ are the Muslim army’s feigned retreat, and the sea is where the Christians’ ships lie: the aim is to cut the Christians off from their ships.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ وَاتَّفَقُو عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْأَمْرِ فِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ ثُمَّ تَجَهَّزُوا وَسَارُوا وَقَدْ أَخَذَ الْحَاجِبُ مَعَهُ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ وَعِشْرِينَ أَلْفًاكَمَا أَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ شَرْكَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu wa-ittafaqū ʿalā dhālika al-amri fī tilka al-sāʿati thumma tajahhazū wa-sārū wa-qad akhadha al-ḥājibu maʿahu al-wazīra dandāna wa-ʿishrīna alfan ka-mā amara al-maliku sharrukānu
sentences.l: And he said to him: With hearing and obedience; and they agreed upon that matter in that hour; then they made-ready and set out, and the chamberlain had taken with him the vizier Dandān and twenty thousand, as the king Sharrukān had commanded.
sentences.i: “With hearing and obedience,” said the chamberlain, and in that hour they agreed on the plan. Then they made ready and set out, the chamberlain having taken with him the vizier Dandān and twenty thousand men, as King Sharrukān had commanded.
sentences.n: The print has واتفقو without the final alif, and runs ألفا and كما together (الفاكما); both kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ رَكِبَ الْقَوْمُ وَهُمْ مُجَرِّدُونَ الصِّفَاحَ وَمُعْتَقِلُونَ الرِّمَاحَ وَحَامِلُونَ السِّلَاحَ وَانْتَشَرَتِ الْخَلَائِقُ فِى الرُّبَا وَالْبِطَاحِ وَصَاحَتِ الْقُسُوسُ وَكُشِفَتِ الرُّؤُسُ وَرُفِعَتِ الصُّلْبَانُ عَلَى قُلُوعِ الْمَرْكَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu rakiba al-qawmu wa-hum mujarridūna al-ṣifāḥa wa-muʿtaqilūna al-rimāḥa wa-ḥāmilūna al-silāḥa wa-intasharati al-khalāʾiqu fī al-rubā wa-al-biṭāḥi wa-ṣāḥati al-qusūsu wa-kushifati al-ruʾūsu wa-rufiʿati al-ṣulbānu ʿalā qulūʿi al-markabi
sentences.l: And when the morning dawned, the people rode, drawing the broad-swords, couching the lances, and bearing the arms; and the multitudes spread over the hills and the wide-valleys, and the priests cried out, and the heads were uncovered, and the crosses were raised upon the sails of the ship.
sentences.i: When morning came the enemy mounted, with swords drawn, lances couched and weapons in hand, and the multitude spread over the hills and the broad valleys. The priests cried out, heads were bared, and crosses were raised on the sails of the ships.
sentences.n: The print has الصباج, a misprint for الصباح, corrected here. مجردون and معتقلون keep their plural ending ـون before an object, as printed (Classical would drop the nūn). الرؤس is the print’s spelling of الرؤوس ‘heads’. المركب is singular in the print, probably for المراكب ‘the ships’; kept as printed and read as a collective, ‘the ships’.

sentences.t: وَقَصَدُوا السَّاحِلَ مِنْ كُلِّ جَانِبٍ وَأَنْزَلُوا الْخَيْلَ فِي الْبَرِّ وَعَزَمُوا عَلَى الْكَرِّ وَالْفَرِّ وَلَمَعَتِ السُّيُوفُ وَتَوَجَّهَتِ الْجُمُوعُ وَبَرَقَتْ شُهُبُ الرِّمَاحِ عَلَى الدُّرُوعِ وَدَارَتْ طَاحُونُ الْمَنَايَا عَلَى رُؤُسِ الرِّجَالِ وَالْفُرْسَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-qaṣadū al-sāḥila min kulli jānibin wa-anzalū al-khayla fī al-barri wa-ʿazamū ʿalā al-karri wa-al-farri wa-lamaʿati al-suyūfu wa-tawajjahati al-jumūʿu wa-baraqat shuhubu al-rimāḥi ʿalā al-durūʿi wa-dārat ṭāḥūnu al-manāyā ʿalā ruʾūsi al-rijāli wa-al-fursāni
sentences.l: And they made for the shore from every side, and brought the horses down on the land, and resolved on the charge and the retreat; and the swords flashed, and the throngs set-themselves-forward, and the meteors of the lances gleamed upon the coats-of-mail, and the mill of the deaths turned upon the heads of the men and the horsemen,
sentences.i: They made for the shore from every side, landed their horses and resolved on attack and retreat. Swords flashed, the hosts advanced, the lances gleamed like shooting stars against the armour, and the mill of death turned above the heads of men and horsemen,
sentences.n: الكرّ والفرّ ‘charge and retreat’ is the stock pair for mounted fighting. طاحون المنايا ‘the mill of the fates’: death is a millstone grinding heads.

sentences.t: وَطَارَتِ الرُّؤُسُ عَنِ الْأَبْدَانِ وَخَرِسَتِ الْأَلْسُنُ وَتَغَشَّتِ الْأَعْيُنُ وَانْفَطَرَتِ الْمَرَائِرُ وَعَمِلَتِ الْبَوَاتِرُ وَطَارَتِ الْجَمَاجِمُ وَقُطِعَتِ الْمَعَاصِمُ وَخَاضَتِ الْخَيْلُ فِى الدِّمَاءِ وَتَقَابَضُوا فِي اللِّحَى
sentences.tr: wa-ṭārati al-ruʾūsu ʿani al-abdāni wa-kharisati al-alsunu wa-taghashshati al-aʿyunu wa-infaṭarati al-marāʾiru wa-ʿamilati al-bawātiru wa-ṭārati al-jamājimu wa-quṭiʿati al-maʿāṣimu wa-khāḍati al-khaylu fī al-dimāʾi wa-taqābaḍū fī al-liḥā
sentences.l: and the heads flew from the bodies, and the tongues went mute, and the eyes were veiled over, and the gall-bladders burst, and the cutting-blades worked, and the skulls flew, and the wrists were cut off, and the horses waded in the blood, and they seized one another by the beards.
sentences.i: heads flew from bodies, tongues fell silent, eyes were clouded, gall-bladders burst, keen blades did their work, skulls flew and wrists were cut through; the horses waded in blood, and men grappled each other by the beards.
sentences.n: المرائر are the gall-bladders (or the stout cords of the heart); bursting is the poet’s phrase for terror.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَتْ عَسَاكِرُ الْإِسْلَامِ بِالصَّلٰوةِ وَالسَّلَامِ عَلَى سَيِّدِ الْأَنَامِ وَبِالثَّنَاءِ عَلَى الرَّحْمَنِ بِمَا أَوْلَى مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥat ʿasākiru al-islāmi bi-al-ṣalāti wa-al-salāmi ʿalā sayyidi al-anāmi wa-bi-al-thanāʾi ʿalā al-raḥmāni bi-mā awlā mina al-iḥsāni
sentences.l: And the armies of Islam cried out with the blessing and the peace upon the lord of mankind, and with the praise of the Merciful for what He bestowed of beneficence.
sentences.i: The armies of Islam cried out blessings and peace upon the master of mankind, and praised the Merciful for the benefits He had bestowed.
sentences.n: الصلوة is the print’s spelling of الصلاة, with the old waw for the long ā. ‘The lord of mankind’ is the Prophet Muḥammad.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَتْ عَسَاكِرُ الْكُفْرِ بِالثَّنَاءِ عَلَى الصَّلِيبِ وَالزَّارِ وَالْعَصِيرِ وَالْعَصَّارِ وَالْقُسُوسِ وَالرُّهْبَانِ وَالسَّعَانِينِ وَالْمُطْرَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥat ʿasākiru al-kufri bi-al-thanāʾi ʿalā al-ṣalībi wa-al-zāri wa-al-ʿaṣīri wa-al-ʿaṣṣāri wa-al-qusūsi wa-al-ruhbāni wa-al-saʿānīni wa-al-muṭrāni
sentences.l: And the armies of unbelief cried out with praise upon the cross, and the zār, and the juice, and the presser, and the priests, and the monks, and the Palm-Sundays, and the metropolitan.
sentences.i: The armies of unbelief cried out in praise of the cross, the girdle, the wine and the winepress, the priests and monks, the feast of Palm Sunday and the metropolitan.
sentences.n: A mocking list of Christian objects. والزار is obscure as printed (perhaps الزنار, the monk’s girdle, with a lost nūn); it is kept as printed and the girdle is given in the idiomatic version as the likelier sense. العصير والعصار ‘the juice and the presser’ is read as the wine of the Eucharist and the press that makes it. السعانين is Palm Sunday.

sentences.t: وَتَأخَّرَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ هُوَ وَشَرْكَانُ إِلَى وَرَائِهِمَا وَقَهْقَرَتِ الْجُيُوشُ وَأَظْهَرُوا الِانْهِزَامَ لِلْأَعْدَاءِ
sentences.tr: wa-taʾakhkhara ḍawʾu al-makāni huwa wa-sharrukānu ilā warāʾihimā wa-qahqarati al-juyūshu wa-aẓharū al-inhizāma li-al-aʿdāʾi
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān held-back, he and Sharrukān, to behind them, and the armies fell back, and they showed the rout to the enemies,
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān and Sharrukān fell back behind their lines, the armies retreated, and the Muslims made a show of flight before the enemy,
sentences.n: The print has ضوء مكان, a misprint for ضوء المكان, corrected here (the article was dropped).

sentences.t: وَزَحَفَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ عَسَاكِرُ الْكُفْرِ لِوَهْمِ الْهَزِيمَةِ وَتَهَيَّئُوا لِلطَّعْنِ وَالضَّرْبِ فَاسْتَهَلَّ أَهْلُ الْإِسْلَامِ بِقِرَأَةِ أَوَّلِ سُورَةِ الْبَقَرَةِ وَصَارَتِ الْقَتْلَى تَحْتَ أَرْجُلِ الْخَيْلِ مُنْدَثِرَهْ
sentences.tr: wa-zaḥafat ʿalayhim ʿasākiru al-kufri li-wahmi al-hazīmati wa-tahayyaʾū li-al-ṭaʿni wa-al-ḍarbi fa-istahalla ahlu al-islāmi bi-qirāʾati awwali sūrati al-baqarati wa-ṣārati al-qatlā taḥta arjuli al-khayli mundathirah
sentences.l: And the armies of unbelief crept upon them, from the imagining of the rout, and made-ready for the thrusting and the striking; and the people of Islam began with the reciting of the beginning of the Sura of the Cow; and the slain were under the feet of the horses, effaced.
sentences.i: The armies of unbelief crept forward, taking the flight for real, and made ready to thrust and strike. The people of Islam began to recite the opening of the Sura of the Cow, while the slain lay trampled under the horses’ feet.
sentences.n: The print has البقر, a misprint for البقرة, corrected here (the closing tāʾ marbūṭa was dropped). The Cow, the second sura of the Qurʾān, is recited here for victory. قرأة is the print’s spelling of قراءة; مندثره is printed with final hāʾ for tāʾ marbūṭa, and is kept as printed.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ مُنَادِى الرُّومِ يَقُولُ يَا عَبَدَةَ الْمَسِيحِ وَذَوِى الدِّينِ الصَّحِيحِ يَا خُدَّامَ الْجَاثَلِيقِ قَدْ لَاحَ لَكُمُ التَّوْفِيقُ إِنَّ عَسَاكِرَ الْإِسْلَامِ قَدْ جَنَحُوا إِلَى الْفِرَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra munādī al-rūmi yaqūlu yā ʿabadata al-masīḥi wa-dhawī al-dīni al-ṣaḥīḥi yā khuddāma al-jāthalīqi qad lāḥa lakumu al-tawfīqu inna ʿasākira al-islāmi qad janaḥū ilā al-firāri
sentences.l: And the crier of the Rūm began saying: O worshippers of the Messiah, and possessors of the sound religion, O servants of the Catholicos, success has appeared to you; truly the armies of Islam have inclined to flight,
sentences.i: The herald of the Rūm began to cry: Servants of the Messiah, men of the true faith, servants of the Catholicos, success is shining on you! The armies of Islam have turned to flee,
sentences.n: الجاثليق is the Catholicos, the Nestorian patriarch; here a generic head of the church. الروم ‘Rūm’ is the Arabic name for the Byzantines and Christians of the West.

sentences.t: فَلَا تُوَلُّوا عَنْهُمُ الْأَدْبَارَ فَمَكِّنُوا السُّيُوفَ مِنْ أَقْفِيَتِهِمْ وَلَا تَرْجِعُوا مِنْ وَرَائِهِمْ وَإِلَّابَرِئْتُمْ مِنَ الْمَسِيحِ ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ الَّذِي فِى الْمَهْدِ تَكَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: fa-lā tuwallū ʿanhumu al-adbāra fa-makkinū al-suyūfa min aqfiyatihim wa-lā tarjiʿū min warāʾihim wa-illā bariʾtum mina al-masīḥi ibni maryama alladhī fī al-mahdi takallama
sentences.l: so do not turn your backs on them; set the swords upon the napes of their necks, and do not turn back from behind them; otherwise you are disowned by the Messiah son of Mary, who spoke in the cradle.
sentences.i: so do not turn your backs on them. Let the swords find their necks, and do not come back from pursuing them, or you are disowned by the Messiah son of Mary, who spoke in the cradle.
sentences.n: The print has تواوا, a misprint for تولوا, corrected here: فلا تولوا عنهم الأدبار echoes the Qurʾān (8:15), ‘do not turn your backs on them’. The print also runs والا and برئتم together (والّابرئتم); the join is kept. The Messiah who ‘spoke in the cradle’ is a Qurʾānic detail (19:29), put on a Christian’s lips here.

sentences.t: وَظَنَّ أَفْرِيدُونُ مَلِكُ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ أَنَّ عَسَاكِرَ الْكُفَّارِ مَنْصُورَةٌ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ حُسْنِ تَدْبِيرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ صُورَةً فَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى مَلِكِ الرُّومِ يُبَشِّرُهُ بِالظَّفَرِ وَيَقُولُ لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ẓanna afrīdūnu maliku al-quṣṭanṭīniyyati anna ʿasākira al-kuffāri manṣūratun wa-lam yaʿlam anna dhālika min ḥusni tadbīri al-muslimīna ṣūratan fa-arsala ilā maliki al-rūmi yubashshiruhu bi-al-ẓafari wa-yaqūlu lahu
sentences.l: And Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople, supposed that the armies of the unbelievers were victorious, and did not know that this was, in form, from the good management of the Muslims; and he sent to the king of the Rūm, giving him good news of the victory, and saying to him:
sentences.i: King Afrīdūn of Constantinople believed that the unbelievers’ armies were winning, and did not see that it was only the look of things, the work of the Muslims’ clever plan. He sent word to the king of the Rūm announcing the victory, and said:

sentences.t: مَا نَفَعَنَا إِلَّا غَائِطُ الْبَطْرِيقِ الْأَكْبَرِ لَمَّا فَاحَتْ رَائِحَتُهُ مِنَ اللِّحَى وَالشَّوَارِبِ بَيْنَ عُبَّادِ الصَّلِيبِ حَاضِرٍ وَغَائِبٍ وَأُقْسِمُ بِالْمُعْجِزَاتِ وَبِبِنْتِهِ أَبْرِيزَةَ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ الْمَرْيَمِيَّةِ وَالْمِيَاهِ الْمَعْمُودِيَّةِ إِنِّي لَا أَتْرُكُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مُجَاهِدًا بِالْكُلِّيَّةِ وَإِنِّي مُصِرٌّ عَلَى سُوءِ هَذِهِ النِّيَّةِ
sentences.tr: mā nafaʿanā illā ghāʾiṭu al-baṭrīqi al-akbari lammā fāḥat rāʾiḥatuhu mina al-liḥā wa-al-shawāribi bayna ʿubbādi al-ṣalībi ḥāḍirin wa-ghāʾibin wa-uqsimu bi-al-muʿjizāti wa-bi-bintihi abrīzata al-naṣrāniyyati al-maryamiyyati wa-al-miyāhi al-maʿmūdiyyati innī lā atruku ʿalā al-arḍi mujāhidan bi-al-kulliyyati wa-innī muṣirrun ʿalā sūʾi hādhihi al-niyyati
sentences.l: Nothing profited us except the excrement of the patriarch the greatest, when its scent wafted from the beards and the moustaches among the worshippers of the cross, present and absent; and I swear by the miracles, and by his daughter Abrīza the Christian, the Marian, and by the baptismal waters, that I will not leave on the earth a fighter-in-the-way at all, and I am persistent in the evil of this intention.
sentences.i: Nothing has helped us but the dung of the Great Patriarch, whose scent rose from beards and moustaches among the worshippers of the cross, near and far. I swear by the miracles, by his daughter Abrīza the Christian, the Marian, and by the baptismal waters: I will not leave a single warrior of the faith alive on earth — I am fixed in this wicked purpose.
sentences.n: The print has واتسم, a misprint for واقسم (the dots of ق put on ت), corrected here: ‘and I swear’, which the following بـ ‘by’ requires. The patriarch’s dung is the same running joke as in the nights before: the Christians treat it as a holy relic, and the Muslim storyteller as a joke. The message is written in the Christian king’s voice and names Abrīza, the patriarch’s daughter, as an oath-object. مجاهدا ‘a fighter in the way of God’ is the word for a Muslim holy warrior.

sentences.t: وَتَوَجَّهَ الرَّسُولُ بِهَذَا الْخِطَابِ ثُمَّ صَاحَ الْكُفَّارُ عَلَى بَعْضِهِمْ قَائِلِينَ خُذُوا بِثَأْرِ لُوقَا
sentences.tr: wa-tawajjaha al-rasūlu bi-hādhā al-khiṭābi thumma ṣāḥa al-kuffāru ʿalā baʿḍihim qāʾilīna khudhū bi-thaʾri lūqā
sentences.l: And the messenger set out with this speech; then the unbelievers cried out to one another, saying: Take vengeance for Lūqā!
sentences.i: The messenger set out with this message. Then the unbelievers shouted to one another: Avenge Lūqā!

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—بَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in every night; the print breaks the last word with a dash (الم—باح).
